C-2.Name: Fix live file-watch delivery: multi-subscriber fan-out in useIpcListener
C-2.Summary: External file changes were not reflected in open Mark tabs (user report: "файл поменялся, а в марке вижу что нет"). The watcher chain (M-003 notify backend → mt::watch::event → M-013-A listener → project.js/editor.js handlers → APPLY_FILE_CHANGE) was fully wired, but useIpcListener registered only the FIRST subscriber's handler per channel — every later watch subscription silently received nothing. C-2 fixes the fan-out and five secondary defects on the same path (leaks, races, a confirm-action crash, a stale stub command), with two sequential clean reviews and 100% coverage of the changed renderer contract files. Amendment 2026-09-21 (follow-up): the now-working live reload exposed a scroll-restore defect — the pre-edit scrollTop was restored unclamped over the reloaded document, parking the viewport past its end (blank until manual scroll); R-9 covers the clamp.

Problem.Description: External file changes do not reflect in open Mark tabs. The chain is unit-tested per link but silently drops events in real sessions with more than one watch subscription.
Problem.RootCause: src/renderer/src/ipc/contract/listener.ts kept ONE Tauri listen() per channel and baked the FIRST subscriber's handler closure into it. Subsequent useIpcListener calls on the same channel only incremented a ref-count; their handlers were never registered. Every ipcWatch.subscribe after the first (second open file, second project root, per-file watch after a project root watch) was a dead subscription. Existing tests only asserted ref-count behavior, never event delivery to a second subscriber, so the defect survived.
Problem.Evidence: listener.ts pre-C-2 (single handler captured at first listen()); contract-listener.test.ts "ref-count increments with multiple subscribers" asserted counts only. Runtime symptom: first watched path live-reloads, all later ones do nothing — no reload, no prompt.

Goals.R-1: Every active useIpcListener subscriber on a channel receives every event payload delivered on that channel (fan-out), regardless of subscription order, while the underlying Tauri listen() stays per-channel single.
Goals.R-2: Disposing one subscriber must not affect delivery to remaining subscribers; disposing the last subscriber tears down the underlying listen(); a later re-subscribe re-establishes delivery. All disposals stay idempotent, including duplicate registration of the same handler reference.
Goals.R-3: ipcWatch.subscribe must not leak a Rust watcher when the listener registration fails after mt::watch::subscribe succeeded (best-effort mt::watch::unsubscribe + rethrow).
Goals.R-4: editor.js _subscribeFileWatch must be race-free: no double subscribe for one pathname (sync pending marker), and a tab closed before the async subscribe resolves must still unsubscribe (deferred dispose).
Goals.R-5: project.js ADD_PROJECT must pass listener:{manual:true} (store-scope subscription; disposal owned by CLOSE_PROJECT as today).
Goals.R-6: Backend mt_close_project_root stops being a no-op stub: it removes the WatchRegistry subscription(s) created for that root path (defense-in-depth; closes the F-WATCH-WIRE-PROJECT TODO in m_v1_compat.rs).
Goals.R-7: liveReloadGenerations entries are removed when the last tab for a pathname closes — independent of whether a per-file watcher entry exists (files inside project trees have none).
Goals.R-8: No behavior change to the documented reload matrix (saved→reload, dirty+liveReload→reload, dirty+no-liveReload→conflict prompt, preview/watch tabs always reload). The conflict prompt's confirm action must work from the watcher path (previously crashed with a TypeError destructuring missing change.data) — pinned by tests/renderer/store/live-reload.test.js.
Goals.R-9: Amendment 2026-09-21 (user-approved follow-up): a live-reload render is a NEW document, so the preserved pre-edit scrollTop must be clamped into the reloaded document's real scrollable range. loadChange stamps the tab (contentReloaded) and the flag rides every file-changed emit that can activate reloaded content (loadChange, UPDATE_CURRENT_FILE, both CLOSE-tab fallbacks, consumed after use); editor.vue clamps, drops leftover first-paint padding before measuring, reveals synchronously, syncs the clamped offset into tab state immediately (no scroll-event debounce dependency), and re-clamps once after the frame. loadChange also drops the tab's stale muya blocks — activation renders tab.blocks verbatim when present (muya setMarkdown blocks-branch), which resurrected the pre-edit document over the reloaded content (defect found by the visual e2e). The same-document restore paths (boot, tab switch back) keep the padding-preserving scrollToCords. Includes the upstream cleanup fix: handleResetPaddingBottom now clears the padding on the element it was set on (#ag-editor-id), not the scroll container. Pinned by tests/renderer/components/editor-coverage.test.js, tests/renderer/store/live-reload.test.js, and tests/e2e/live-reload-scroll.spec.ts (visual gate: new-document text inside the viewport with no user scroll, no phantom padding) — V-M-011 scenario-29.

Constraints.Constraint: BLOCK_LISTENER_REFCOUNT marker semantics preserved: one log line per subscribe/unsubscribe with the subscriber count.
Tauri command arg naming (camelCase JS ↔ snake_case Rust) unchanged.
WatchRegistry stays process-global Tauri-managed state; unsubscribe remains idempotent by sub id and by path.

100% line+branch coverage required for the changed renderer contract files (listener.ts, watch.ts) and for every changed function in store files; all new/changed Rust code paths covered by deterministic tests. Coverage is enforced by scoped runs, NOT by raising the global vitest thresholds (repo-wide values stay at the measured baseline).
Two sequential independent reviews (different angles) must both return clean before the change ships: review-1 correctness/races/edge-cases, review-2 security/contracts/regressions.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Symlink canonicalization (/tmp vs /private/tmp) between notify-reported paths and store pathnames — documented known limitation, separate change if it ever bites in practice.
Redesigning the reload matrix, watcher ignore-self-echo on save (already handled via hash-skip), or project-tree refresh semantics.
Linux/Windows watcher coverage (macOS-only product at this phase).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Two subscriptions on mt::watch::event each receive their own events (subscriptionId-filtered) regardless of order; pinned by contract-listener.test.ts fan-out tests.
listener.ts and watch.ts report 100% statements/branches/functions/lines in scoped coverage runs.
Full renderer suite green (npm test), typecheck:ipc clean, cargo test green; CI coverage gate (npm run test:coverage with baseline thresholds) passes.

Runtime proof on the real app: two files opened, the SECOND externally modified live-reloads ([editor][live_reload][BLOCK_LIVE_RELOAD source=disk] for both paths; [FsWatcher] register/coalesce markers in stderr).
grace lint --assertions current reports zero C-2-attributable errors.
Review-1 and review-2 both return VERDICT: CLEAN.

AffectedAreas.M-032: editor store: watch-subscribe races, generations cleanup, conflict-prompt confirm fix (editor.js)
AffectedAreas.M-036: project store: manual listener flag for the root watcher (project.js)
AffectedAreas.M-011: editor surface: scrollToCordsAfterReload reload clamp + handleResetPaddingBottom element fix (editor.vue) — R-9 amendment

Governance: V-M-013-A scenario-5 (fan-out) and V-M-003 scenario-4 + stop_path markers in .grace/verification/runtime.xml.
